app/src/lib/api.ts:22 — references undefined `res` in the !response.ok branch; the exact class of error type-checking would catch (emitted as-is in dist/server/chunk/document.js:13)
app/src/lib/api.ts:6-11 — ApiError is dead code; the intended status-carrying error is never thrown
app/src/lib/data.ts:24,82,167 — api<any>(...) / (entry: any) throughout the data layer; no PokeAPI schema types at the boundary

app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:56-60, moves/[name].ts:30-36, abilities/[name].ts:33-37, types/[name].ts:29-34, 404.ts:10-14 — the same not-found template copy-pasted five times, while app/src/lib/components.ts:43 exports an unused notFound() helper
app/src/lib/data.ts:78-80 — per-card /pokemon/<id>/ fan-out (mapLimit 40) for potentially hundreds of cards on move/type/ability pages
app/src/routes/abilities/[name].ts:19 — .catch(() => null) at the route instead of the tryApi convention used everywhere else (app/src/lib/api.ts:40)
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access and config are well centralized and a framework upgrade would touch few files, but the codebase has no type-checking safety net at all (no tsconfig, no check script, `any` at every boundary), leans on undocumented framework pipeline behavior for asset URLs, and copy-pastes markup that a shared helper was written for.

findings.issue: `throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status} ${res.statusText}`)` references an undefined `res` (the parameter is `response`); the failure path throws a ReferenceError instead of the intended error, and ApiError (api.ts:6) is never used.
findings.suggestion: Use `response`, and throw `new ApiError(response.status, url)` — i.e. actually use the ApiError class; add a `check` script (tsc) so this class of bug is caught before runtime.

findings.issue: No tsconfig.json, no `typescript`/`@types/node`, and no type-check script: TypeScript is transpile-only, so the framework's typed `defineRoute`/handler contracts and the app's own types are never verified (Gracile ships `@gracile/gracile/tsconfigs/base.json` and its starters include a `check` script).
findings.suggestion: Add a tsconfig extending `@gracile/gracile/tsconfigs/base.json`, install typescript + @types/node, and add `"check": "tsc"` to scripts (as the official starters do).

findings.issue: Asset URLs are computed at runtime via `new URL('./document.css', import.meta.url).pathname`; the emitted server chunk still contains that expression (dist/server/chunk/document.js:13), which in production resolves to a filesystem path and only works because the framework's `injectServerAssets` step strips the tag and re-injects the built asset — undocumented, fragile behavior.
findings.suggestion: Reference assets statically as the docs do (e.g. `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/src/document.css" />`), letting the Gracile/Vite client build rewrite them to hashed URLs.

findings.issue: Server-side `fetch(url)` has no AbortSignal/timeout and no HTTP caching headers; one hung API request hangs the page render indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Use `fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) })` and treat 404/5xx distinctly (via the currently-dead ApiError) so unknown resources 404 cleanly.

findings.issue: The entire data layer is `any`-typed (`api<any>(...)`, `(entry: any)`, `(row: any)`), so changes to the API's shape — which the spec explicitly says happen — surface only at request time.
findings.suggestion: Declare interfaces for the PokeAPI resources actually consumed (species, pokemon, type, move, ability, generation) and type `api<T>()` at each call site.

findings.issue: The not-found markup is copy-pasted in five places (pokemon, moves, abilities, types routes and 404.ts) even though `app/src/lib/components.ts:43` already exports an unused `notFound()` helper.
findings.suggestion: Delete the duplicates and use the existing `notFound()` component (or a shared route-level notFound template) in all five spots.

findings.issue: Dead exports: `getAbility` (data.ts:139), `sectionHeading` (components.ts:50), `notFound` (components.ts:43), `ApiError` (api.ts:6) — code that looks load-bearing but is never called.
findings.suggestion: Remove them, or wire them in where they were clearly intended (notFound into the routes, ApiError into api()).

findings.issue: Inconsistent error handling: this route wraps `getAbilityPage` in `.catch(() => null)`, while every other route uses the `tryApi` convention (api.ts:40) — two ways to say the same thing.
findings.suggestion: Have `getAbilityPage` use `tryApi` like its siblings and drop the route-level catch.

findings.issue: Per-card `/pokemon/<id>/` fan-out (mapLimit 40) means move/type/ability pages issue hundreds of sequential-ish upstream requests on first render; only the URL-level promise cache softens repeat visits.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable given the runtime cache, but consider a larger concurrency limit, request coalescing, or deriving card data from list endpoints where the API allows it.

summary: The app is squarely on the framework's current generation — current Gracile APIs, the documented Hono adapter setup, lean modern dependencies, and platform-first client code — so an upgrade would touch few files. It will not age well at the edges though: TypeScript is transpile-only with `any` everywhere and no type-check step, which has already produced a real bug (`res` is undefined in the API error path), plus an undocumented asset-URL trick and five copies of the not-found markup. Framework usage is exemplary; the typing and error-handling discipline is what a future maintainer pays for.
